newsitem.title: USA: Ohio's corn four percent harvested vs. 10 average.
newsitem.headline: Ohio's corn four percent harvested vs. 10 average.

text.p: Ohio's corn crop was four percent harvested as of Sunday, down from 10 percent for the five year average, the Agricultural Satistics Service said in its weekly crop report.
Corn was rated four percent very poor, 14 percent poor, 42 percent fair, 35 percent good and five percent excellent.
Soybean harvest was two percent complete and 40 percent of the plants were dropping leaves, versus 95 percent average.
Soybeans were rated four percent very poor, 15 percent poor, 41 percent fair, 35 percent good and five percent excellent.
Light frost was reported in low-lying areas last week but little damage was noted, the report said.

"The crops look good but there are still some fields around that are green and immature," the report said. "An early hard frost would cause some acreage of both (corn and soybeans) to be completely lost or greatly reduced in yield."
Topsoil moisture was rated four percent very short, 14 percent short, 66 percent adequate and 16 percent surplus.
Pasture and range were rated four percent very poor, 19 percent poor, 39 percent fair, 36 percent good and two percent excellent.
